Simulate a Complete UNO Game

play_game.Rd

Runs a full UNO game simulation from setup to finish, returning the final game outcome. Internally, this function calls setup_game to initialize the deck, deal cards, and configure play direction and turn order. It then executes the gameplay loop using play_turns_loop until one player wins by discarding all their cards.

Usage

play_game(n_players = 4)

Arguments

n_players

Integer. Number of players to simulate (default is 4).
This version supports any number of players ≥2, based on deck capacity.
Note: In future versions of the package, we plan to expand support for larger groups with rule adaptations, deck validation, and team-based formats.

Value

A named list with the final game results:

  • winner – Character. Name of the winning player (e.g., "Player_1").

  • hands – Named list of tibbles representing each player’s final hand. Only the winner will have an empty hand.

  • discard – Tibble showing the full discard pile used throughout the game.

Details

This function is the most user-friendly entry point and is ideal for batch simulations, gameplay testing, educational demos, or scoring.

This function performs two main stages:

  • Game initialization – setup_game shuffles the deck, deals hands, and sets turn order.

  • Gameplay loop – play_turns_loop simulates turns until one player wins.

The result can be passed to score_game for post-game analysis and ranking.

Examples

# Run a complete game
result <- play_game(n_players = 4)
#> Player_3 wins!

# Extract winner
result$winner
#> [1] "Player_3"

# Check final card counts per player
sapply(result$hands, nrow)
#> Player_1 Player_2 Player_3 Player_4 
#>        4        2        0        2 

# View last card played
tail(result$discard)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   color value   type  
#>   <chr> <chr>   <chr> 
#> 1 blue  9       number
#> 2 blue  5       number
#> 3 blue  6       number
#> 4 blue  reverse action
#> 5 green reverse action
#> 6 green 7       number

# Score and rank players
score_game(result)
#> Player_3 Player_2 Player_4 Player_1 
#>        0        2        2        4
